title: FRB20190605B has a higher later two-band fraction in 54 normalized-data tests with small DM changes
abstract: We test intensity data for two CHIME bursts selected by an earlier catalog-fit study. In FRB20190605B, the later minus earlier high-band fraction is 0.1830, with a 95 percent noise-perturbation interval of 0.1287 to 0.2399. All 54 normalized-data tests with changes of at most 0.1 pc cm^-3 in dispersion measure give a positive difference. A guarded calibration test also retains positive estimates. Unguarded calibration is unstable because some channel conversion factors are very large. The other target, FRB20181222E, gives no stable positive result. Changes of 1 pc cm^-3 can reverse direction. The result tests spectral shape in fixed endpoint windows and a fixed mask. It does not establish continuous drift, intrinsic emission physics, or independent telescope confirmation. Code, hashes, a statistical figure and separate-scratch retrieval steps are supplied. External source arrays and trial records are excluded.

display.caption: Blue marks show the primary normalized two-band contrast and its 95 percent noise-perturbation interval. Orange lines show the range in 54 small-DM normalized controls. The weak later pulse of FRB20181222E makes its ratio interval unstable. These are observed response measures, not intrinsic energy fractions.
